description: The staple of the hills: dense, dark flatbread of nagli (finger millet/ragi), patted thick and roasted on clay or iron, eaten with garlic-chilli chutney, curd or whatever the season's shaak is. Nagli grows on Dang's rain-fed slopes and carries the region's nutrition on its back, iron-rich, filling, and at its best hot off a village chulha with white butter. Homestay and campsite meals serve it as a matter of course; ask for it at small eateries and you'll be understood immediately.
cultural_note: Nagli is the crop of the adivasi hill farm. The rotla is everyday food, not a restaurant invention, and being offered one at a home is straightforward hospitality.

images.caption: A Dangi thali at Nahari Restaurant, Ahwa, nagli rotla with kadhi, dal, shaak, papad and rice
